2027-04-26.title: Monday of the Fifth Week of Easter
readings: We bring you good news, that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God
Not to us, O Lord, but to your name give the glory (or: Alleluia)
The Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything
2027-04-26.alt: Easter weekday of the fifth week (Year I). The Alleluia is sung before the Gospel, the Paschal candle stays lit beside the ambo, and the Regina Caeli takes the place of the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-26.verse: Jesus answered him, “Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.”
theo: Paul and Barnabas are on their first missionary journey, in the hill country of Lycaonia in the middle of what is now Turkey. Threatened in Iconium, they move on to Lystra, and there they meet a man “who could not use his feet and had never walked, for he had been crippled from birth.” He listens to Paul preaching, and Paul, “looking at him intently and seeing that he had faith to be healed,” calls out: “Stand upright on your feet.” The man springs up and walks. Then something unexpected happens. The crowd shouts in their own language, “The gods have come down to us in human form!” They call Barnabas Zeus and Paul Hermes, “because he was the chief speaker,” and the priest of Zeus arrives with oxen and garlands to offer sacrifice. The people of that region told an old story of Zeus and Hermes once visiting in disguise and going unrecognised; perhaps they did not want to make that mistake again. The apostles tear their clothes and rush into the crowd: “Friends, why are you doing this? We are mortals just like you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.” Paul's first sermon to pure pagans does not begin with the Law of Moses but with creation: God “has not left himself without a witness in doing good,” for he gives “rains from heaven and fruitful seasons,” filling people “with food and your hearts with joy.” The Psalm gives the apostles' answer in one line: “Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory.”

In the Gospel we are back at the Last Supper. Jesus has promised to show himself to those who love him, and Judas, “not Iscariot,” asks a fair question: “Lord, how is it that you will reveal yourself to us, and not to the world?” Jesus does not answer with a spectacle. He answers with a dwelling: “Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.” The people of Lystra wanted gods who would come down for a visit and be honoured with oxen. The true God does far more: the Father and the Son come to stay, in the heart of the one who loves and obeys. And they do not leave us to remember everything by our own strength: “the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.” St Augustine, looking back on the years he searched for God outside himself, wrote (in substance): you were within me, and I was outside, looking for you there. In these last weeks before Pentecost the Church asks us to look within, where the Holy Trinity has made a home.
outline: Ask: when people praise you, where does the glory go?
The apostles refuse worship and point to the living God.
Rain, harvests and joy speak of the Creator.
Point 3 · We will make our home with them
The Trinity dwells in the one who loves; the Spirit teaches and reminds.
“We will come to them and make our home with them.”
live: When you are praised today, say inwardly: not to me, Lord, but to your name.
Spend five quiet minutes tonight with the Lord who lives in you, and ask the Holy Spirit to remind you of one word of Jesus.
2027-04-26.prayer: Living God, maker of heaven and earth and sea, you have never left yourself without a witness: you send the rain, you ripen the harvest, you fill our hearts with joy. Not to us, Lord, but to your name be the glory. Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, come with the Father and make your home in us; and send us the Holy Spirit, the Advocate, to teach us everything and remind us of all you have said. Amen.
altar: The God the people of Lystra mistook for a passing visitor comes to stay. In Holy Communion the risen Lord truly enters the one who receives him, Body and Blood, soul and divinity, so that the promise “we will make our home with them” takes flesh in us.

quick: At Lystra Paul healed a man crippled from birth, and the crowd tried to worship Paul and Barnabas as gods.
The apostles refused: we are mortals like you; turn to the living God who gives rain and joy.
Jesus promises that the Father and the Son will make their home in those who love him, and the Spirit will teach them.
2027-04-26.action: Each time you are thanked or praised today, pass it on to God with a silent “Glory to you, Lord.”
2027-04-26.question: Is my heart a home where the Father and the Son are welcome to stay?

family.explain: When Paul healed a man who could not walk, people thought Paul was a god and wanted to offer him a sacrifice. Paul said: no! I am a person like you. Thank the real God, who sends rain and food and joy. Jesus tells us that if we love him, God comes to live in our hearts, like a guest who stays.
family.intention: We pray for farmers waiting for the monsoon rains, and for everyone who has no food on the table.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make our heart, and our home, a nice place for Jesus to stay?”

illus: St Teresa of Kolkata was often praised as a living saint. She used to answer (in substance): I am only a little pencil in the hand of God; he does the writing. Nobody admires a pencil, she would say, only what is written. Like Paul and Barnabas at Lystra, she turned every garland back towards God.

pm.open: Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory. Come and make your home in us. Amen.
share: We are mortals just like you (Acts 14:15). How do I handle praise, and do I let it point to God?
He has not left himself without a witness in doing good (Acts 14:17). Where did I see God's goodness in creation this week?
We will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:23). What would change if I really believed God lives in me?
pm.resp: Not to us, O Lord, but to your name give the glory.
interc: For missionaries who bring the Gospel to people who have never heard it, that they may speak with humility and joy.
For all who are disabled from birth, and for their families and carers.
For farmers and for good rains in the coming monsoon.
For leaders and celebrities who are flattered and praised, that they may not take God's place.
For our group, that the Holy Spirit may teach us and remind us of the words of Jesus.
pm.close: Father, with your Son you come to dwell in those who love you. Keep our hearts open to you, through the Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, at Lystra a man crippled from birth listens to Paul, and Paul sees that he has faith to be healed. Stand upright on your feet! The man springs up and walks (Acts 14:10). And the crowd goes wild: the gods have come down to us in human form! They bring oxen and garlands to worship Paul and Barnabas.

This was a great temptation. Who would not enjoy being treated as a god? But the apostles tear their clothes and run into the crowd: we are mortals just like you (Acts 14:15). They point away from themselves to the living God, who sends rain from heaven and fruitful seasons and fills hearts with joy. The best witness is a finger that points beyond itself.

In the Gospel Jesus tells us what the true God really does. Not a short visit to be honoured with sacrifices, but a dwelling: those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:23). The Father and the Son make their home in an ordinary heart that loves and obeys.

And we are not left alone to remember everything. The Holy Spirit, the Advocate, will teach you everything and remind you of all that I have said (John 14:26). In these days of Easter, as Pentecost comes near, let us give every glory back to God, and keep a quiet room in our hearts for the Guest who has come to stay. Amen.
kids: Children, Paul healed a man who had never walked, and the people thought Paul was a god! But Paul said: no, I am just a person like you. Thank God! Jesus says something wonderful: if you love me, my Father and I will come and live in your heart. So your heart can be God's little house. Keep it clean and happy for him!

intro: Theme: “We will come to them and make our home with them.”
Apostles who refuse worship, a Creator who never leaves himself without witness, and a God who comes to stay.

sub: A witness points away from himself.
q: Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.

Friends, why are you doing this? We are mortals just like you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these worthless things to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them.
points.apply: This week, whenever you succeed or are praised, say aloud or in your heart: not to us, Lord, but to your name.

q: The heavens are telling the glory of God; and the firmament proclaims his handiwork.
Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature, invisible though they are, have been understood and seen through the things he has made.
points.apply: Before each meal this week, name one gift of creation on your plate and thank the Creator for it.

points.h: We will make our home with them
sub: Not a visit but a dwelling.
q: My dwelling place shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Jesus answered him, “Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.”
points.apply: Each night until Pentecost, end the day with a minute of silence before the God who lives in you, and pray: Come, Holy Spirit.

concl: The apostles at Lystra refused to be gods so that people might find the true God.
That God does not visit and leave: with the Father and the Spirit, the risen Jesus makes his home in those who love him.
2027-04-26.resolve: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” each evening from now until Pentecost.
